summary: Faroese succession law follows the Danish model, which protects children with a forced share, but the exact rules were not confirmed. The Faroes have no trust law and are outside the Hague Trusts Convention. Foundations exist under Faroese law.
reserved_share: Children are forced heirs under the Danish-based Faroese succession rules; the fraction (believed 1/4 of the estate in Denmark) was not confirmed for the Faroes.
foreign_law_note: Nordic conflict rules look to the deceased's domicile; whether foreign law may be chosen in the Faroes was not confirmed.
trust_note: No trust law; Denmark is not party to the Hague Trusts Convention and it is not extended to the Faroes. Faroese law has its own foundation rules.
open_questions: Which Faroese inheritance act applies and its forced share; no source was found.
Foreign-law choice under Faroese conflict rules.
Whether a family foundation is allowed and how it is taxed.
